land.text: Bonny, under a protectorate treaty of February 1886 ('in 1886 assuming control under a protectorate treaty')

successors.note: The Niger Coast Protectorate page has the Oil Rivers Protectorate established in 1884; the Bonny page gives February 1886 for the treaty. The kingdom continues as a traditional state with a king today.

land.text: Opobo, founded by Jaja after the 1869 battle in Bonny

capitals.name: Bonny
capitals.note: Approximate coordinates (the page gives no capital and no coordinates); the page has the kingdom beginning at Orupiri, 'Bonny Island'.

correction.text: Bonny Island and its mainland and hinterland segments: neighbours Kalabari, Nembe and Okrika

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives no area or frontier; a 20 km circle on Bonny Island stands for the city-state. 'Bonny became important in the 15th century with the arrival of the Portuguese'.

correction.text: Bonny after the split that created Opobo in 1869

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the same circle; Jaja's party took Opobo (a separate state).

ledger.note: c. 1000: the Bonny kingdom. 'The kingdom was founded before or about 1000 AD' at Orupiri on Bonny Island; Alagbariya is named as founder. The page's dating is a tradition; 'Bonny became important in the 15th century with the arrival of the Portuguese'.

1869: Jaja founds Opobo. 'In 1869 a major battle between the two factions led to Ja-Ja founding a new state at Opobo' (the Opobo page dates his arrival to 1870, and his rule from 25 December 1870); the British consul intervened in 1873 and 1882.

1886 (February): Bonny signs a protectorate treaty. 'In February 1886 a protectorate treaty was concluded between Bonny and Britain.' King George had been deposed on 14 December 1883 and died in October 1888.
1886 (February): sovereign Bonny ends; the kingdom continues as a traditional state (Edward Asimini William Dappa Pepple III took the throne in 1996).

wars.name: Bonny civil war and the founding of Opobo
wars.outcome: A major battle between the two factions in 1869 led to Jaja founding Opobo; British intervention in 1873 and 1882.
wars.note: The page does not name it a war; the Opobo page dates the move to 1870.

sources.title: Bonny Kingdom
sources.note: Founded before or about 1000 AD; Portuguese 15th century; Pepple kings 1830-1888; 1869 battle and Opobo; 1873 and 1882 interventions; protectorate treaty February 1886; no area, capital or extent.

sources.title: Opobo
sources.note: Jaja arrived in 1870 after the Bonny civil war; ruled from 25 December 1870.

notes: The Bonny Kingdom has no Cliopatria row. Two pages opened; neither gives an area, a capital or an extent (Imo River, Andoni and the Oil Rivers Protectorate are not mentioned), so the 20 km circle on Bonny Island and the capital dot (about 4.44 N 7.17 E) are placeholders. The 1000 start is the page's tradition ('before or about 1000 AD'). The pages disagree on the Opobo move: 1869 (Bonny) vs 1870 (Opobo). The Niger Coast Protectorate page puts the Oil Rivers protectorate in 1884; the Bonny page has its treaty in 1886. Not placed: Kalabari, Nembe and Okrika (named neighbours), the slave-to-palm-oil trade after 1807.
